themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 216 THIS WEEK—a 704% increase over the 8-week baseline of 26.9 per week—suggesting rapid deterioration of roads across Hillcrest/Fresh Meadows, coinciding with complaints about curb conditions (up 700% last week) and street sweeping failures (up 700% last week).
evidence: Street Condition complaints: 216 THIS WEEK vs. 26.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 24.0)
Curb Condition complaints: 18 last week vs. 2.2 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 6.75)
Street Sweeping complaints: 7 last week vs. 0.9 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 6.61)
DOB alteration filings remain elevated at 256 of 487 total permits, suggesting ongoing construction disruptions
reporting_angles: Ground-truth assessment: Drive/walk the neighborhoods experiencing the highest complaints to document potholes, debris, degradation
Sanitation department response: Interview DSNY about street sweeping delays and why complaints spiked so dramatically
Infrastructure maintenance backlog: Cross-reference with DOE/DSNY budget allocation—is this district being deprioritized?

themes_detail.label: Food poisoning outbreak signal
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK—a 2300% increase from the 0.1 weekly average—a potential early warning sign of foodborne illness cluster in the district; warrants immediate health department follow-up.
evidence: Food Poisoning complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69, 2300% spike)
Spike is statistically significant and unprecedented in the baseline period
No corresponding Reddit discussions or news coverage yet—this may be an unreported developing story
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene: Are they investigating? Which restaurants/facilities are implicated?
Affected residents: Interview the complainants (via 311 follow-up) to identify common source and symptom timeline
Restaurant inspection records: Cross-reference recent violations or closures in the district

themes_detail.label: Commercial noise surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints reached 5 THIS WEEK—a 1233% jump from the 0.4 weekly average—suggesting new commercial activity, construction, or venue opening disrupting residential areas.
evidence: Noise - Commercial complaints: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 9.55, 1233% spike)
No prior pattern of commercial noise issues in the 90-day dataset
Multiple active ULURP rezonings in pipeline (St. Francis Prep, 164th Street, Union Turnpike, Queens Boulevard) may indicate new commercial development triggering violations
reporting_angles: Identify the source: Which business(es) or construction site(s) are generating the complaints? Cross-reference with active DOB permits.
Development connection: Are the St. Francis Prep or 164th Street rezoning projects generating construction noise ahead of approval?
Resident impact: Interview affected residents about noise type, timing, and duration

themes_detail.label: Building code violations uptick
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints jumped to 27 last week—a 248% increase from the 7.8 weekly average—coupled with ongoing elevated General Construction/Plumbing complaints (22 three weeks ago, 117% above baseline), suggesting inadequate building inspections during the current development surge (487 permits filed in 90 days).
evidence: Building/Use complaints: 27 last week vs. 7.8 weekly average (248% spike, z-score: 5.82)
General Construction/Plumbing complaints: 22 three weeks ago vs. 10.1 weekly average (117% spike, z-score: 6.25)
487 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (256 alterations, 71 new buildings) suggests sustained construction activity
Community Board has repeatedly requested additional building inspectors—unmet need appears to be manifesting in complaint surge
reporting_angles: DOB capacity crisis: Interview DOB leadership about inspector staffing levels and permit review backlogs in CD 408
Community Board budget request follow-up: Why has the standing request for additional building inspectors not been funded?
Resident complaints deep dive: Survey recent Building/Use complainants to identify common violations (unpermitted work, unsafe conditions, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Sanitation worker complaints
themes_detail.summary: Sanitation worker/vehicle complaints spiked to 7 two weeks ago—a 1020% increase from the 0.6 weekly average—indicating service quality or worker conduct issues; coupled with street sweeping and curb complaints, suggests systemic sanitation department failures.
evidence: Sanitation Worker/Vehicle complaints: 7 two weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 13.17, 1020% spike)
Clustered with Street Sweeping spike (7 last week, 700% above baseline) and Curb Condition spike (18 last week, 700% above baseline)
Pattern suggests either understaffing, route changes, or conduct issues at DSNY
reporting_angles: DSNY staffing and scheduling: Interview sanitation department about staffing levels, route changes, or scheduling disruptions
Complaint details: What specific worker or vehicle misconduct is being reported? (Negligence, rudeness, equipment issues?)
Resident interviews: Talk to complainants about the nature of sanitation failures and impact on neighborhood cleanliness
